target_customer: Mobile players, mostly teens and young adults, who want a social avatar world; plus creators and brands building inside it
problem: People wanted a persistent, social virtual world on mobile where they could dress avatars, decorate spaces, and hang out, with user-created content.
business_model: Free-to-play with in-app purchases of avatar items; later a creator earn program (Highrise Earn Program, 2024)
product_category: Mobile social virtual world / UGC gaming

founders.name: Jimmy Xu
founders.background_notes: Says he spent nine years working on mainstream virtual worlds (YC page).

technical_complexity.rationale: A real-time multiplayer 3D social world with avatars and UGC on phones is standard game-engineering with hard scaling parts, built by a small team with a Unity base.

defensibility.rationale: Social graph, avatar items users own and a creator community create stickiness, but virtual world formats are copyable and users migrate between games.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing an incumbent copying or buying Highrise; instead Pocket Worlds became the acquirer (Everskies in 2021, Infinite Canvas in January 2025, Hotel Hideaway in September 2026 per the YC page).

market_need_then: Highrise was already live as an iOS beta in 2015 and the YC page reports it had grown to many millions of users, indicating pull from young mobile users; the January 2021 article cites over 7 million users and six-fold growth in the previous year.

branding.domain_note: pocketworlds.com for the company; highrise.game for the product.

identity.voice_and_tone: Casual, creator-friendly; CEO pitches 'every brand or community having a Reddit, a Discord, and a Highrise' per a profile

branding.brand_signature: Highrise as the avatar-and-apartment social world with a creator ecosystem
branding.community_and_virality: YC Tech Talk 'MMOs in the Instagram Era' (2020), a creator program and Highrise Studio (Highrise 4.0, 2024), and a Neopets crossover covered by trade press; 'Highrise' also collides with the unrelated Project Highrise building game (2018).

brand_strength.rationale: Product name Highrise is simple and memorable and the product reached tens of millions of registered users with a visible creator program, but 'Highrise' is a generic word that overlaps with an unrelated game and Pocket Worlds as a company brand is lightly sourced.

outcome_analysis: Pocket Worlds' Highrise was an iOS beta in 2015, joined YC in Summer 2018, hit Android in January 2020 during the pandemic, and raised a $7M Series A led by Bitkraft in January 2021 when it reportedly had over 7 million users. It then used that base to buy Everskies (2021), Infinite Canvas (January 2025) and Hotel Hideaway (September 2026, per the YC page) and reports 50 million-plus registered users, so it is a durable independent winner with no exit; the funding record is thin and later rounds are not found, so scale of capital raised is uncertain.
notes: Series A $7M confirmed by Game Developer (2021-01-28) and PocketGamer.biz, two outlets. Aggregators disagree on totals ($7M to $10.1M) and list an earlier seed with Canaan Partners and a GREE VR Capital entry; those are unverified and not recorded as rounds. Highrise predates the batch (iOS beta March 2015 per Wikipedia; one source says 2016 and another 2019 for mobile launch). Founded 2013 per YC page. Everskies acquisition in 2021 comes from Wikipedia and a search summary; the date within 2021 and price were not found. Competition: no source dated near 2018 naming competitors was found (a search for IMVU, Second Life and Avakin Life returned nothing dated), so the list is empty. The 2025 and 2026 dates rely on trade press and the YC page. Name origins not found. Web Archive skipped.
